title: HexOct: Knitting Crystals: a knitted HexOct fabric, its construction, mechanics and comfort for every close-packed stacking
description:
Version 4. DICTO proposed a fabric that is a crystal: one continuous multi-layer knitted fabric whose knitted sheets are the close-packed layers of balls and whose linking yarns join each node to the three nodes of the next sheet that its ball touches, turning on in the same sense at a c layer and back at an h layer. The cells it closes off are the pieces of the HexOct tiles (#75), so any close-packed stacking can be knitted into the fabric's own thickness.

Main result. In the idealised Knitted HexOct all stackings have the same density; compression, buckling onset, rigidity, vapour transfer, conduction along the yarn and direct radiation through twelve sheets are the same in every stacking. The stacking changes only the straight see-through area (up to 10.7 times larger in 2H than in 3C) and, when the sheets are much softer than the links, the free transverse shear (3C up to 17.5 times softer than 2H), set by the stack's net turning, not by the share of c layers.

Contents. Front section with the comfort results (Part 3); Part 1, construction specification (geometry, yarn and stitch plan by hand and by machine, two test pieces); Part 2, lattice mechanics and a see-through proxy.

Version history. Versions 1–2 knitted an edge-on slice of the stackings as a flat pattern; Version 3 withdrew them for this revision; Version 4 presents the Knitted HexOct itself. The fabric has not yet been knitted; the knitted test pieces will be added in a later version.

The Knitted HexOct, its idea and its name are DICTO's; design, computation, checks and drafting with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0.
